items.title: AMD Just Crushed Nvidia by 32 Points After Scandal. Here’s How NVDA Can Come Back
items.summary: One chipmaker just posted its best five-day run against its rival since 1999, while the other faces a CEO scandal and a Senate spotlight. Three scorecard categories decide which stock deserves retirement money, and the loser might surprise you.

items.title: AMD Just Beat Nvidia by the Widest Margin Since 1999
items.summary: One chipmaker posted record results and landed marquee cloud customers. Its biggest rival lost its CEO and stumbled again. The week produced a split no one has seen in 27 years, and the aftermath may be messier than the headline suggests.

items.title: Harvard Cut Nvidia by a Third and Bought AMD
items.summary: Harvard's endowment rotated inside AI chips just before a brutal selloff hit one of them. Since then, the two stocks have moved very differently, and a closer look at the filing shows who really came out ahead.

items.title: Why Advanced Micro Devices Stock Surged This Week

items.title: Arista Grew 58.5% Last Quarter: Does Nvidia’s CEO Exit Make It a Buy, or a Risk?
items.summary: Key TakeawaysJensen Huang resigned as Nvidia’s CEO on November 12, and chip stocks like AMD and Broadcom fell sharply. That puts Arista Networks’ pitch of working with many chip vendors in the spotlight.

items.title: Review & Preview: Moving On

items.title: Wall Street stocks mostly lower as Nvidia extends slump
items.summary: Wall Street stocks mostly fell Friday as tech shares remained under pressure following the shock downfall of Nvidia's chief Jensen Huang, while the dollar rose following additional data that showed US inflation is persisting."There is certainly a defensive leadership as we look at the sectors, which points to some caution," said Kourkafas, who expects AI to be in the spotlight again next week when Nvidia reports quarterly results and Anthropic makes its Wall Street debut.
